plugin.gf256.title: GF(2⁸) calculator (AES field arithmetic)
plugin.gf256.param.opHint: xtime multiplies a by x ({02}), multiplication computes a • b, inverse computes a⁻¹.
plugin.gf256.param.aHint: Exactly one byte as two hex digits, e.g. 57.
plugin.gf256.param.bHint: Exactly one byte as two hex digits; only used by the multiplication, xtime and the inverse ignore it.
plugin.gf256.region.shifted: a shifted left (9 bits, not reduced)
plugin.gf256.op.shift: Shift – move every bit one place to the left
plugin.gf256.op.reduce: Reduce – XOR with the irreducible polynomial if bit 8 is set
plugin.gf256.op.xtime: xtime – multiply the addend by x
plugin.gf256.op.add: Add – XOR the addend into the accumulator
plugin.gf256.op.skip: Skip – this bit of b is 0
plugin.gf256.op.multiply: Multiply the running power by a
plugin.gf256.step.xtime.load: We multiply a = {{a}} by x, i.e. by {02}.
plugin.gf256.step.xtime.shiftCarry: Shifting {{a}} one bit to the left gives {{shifted}}: bit 7 was 1, so it is carried out into bit 8.
plugin.gf256.step.xtime.shiftNoCarry: Shifting {{a}} one bit to the left gives {{shifted}}: bit 7 was 0, so nothing is carried out.
plugin.gf256.step.xtime.reduce: Bit 8 is set, so we XOR with the irreducible polynomial {11b}: xtime({{a}}) = {{result}}.
plugin.gf256.step.xtime.noReduce: Bit 8 is clear, so no reduction is needed: xtime({{a}}) = {{result}}.
plugin.gf256.step.gmul.load: We multiply a = {{a}} by b = {{b}}: for each set bit i of b we add a • xⁱ to an accumulator that starts at {00}.
plugin.gf256.step.gmul.xtimeShift: a • x^{{bit}} = xtime({{previous}}): bit 7 is 0, so a plain left shift gives {{addend}}.
plugin.gf256.step.gmul.xtimeReduce: a • x^{{bit}} = xtime({{previous}}): bit 7 is 1, so we shift left and XOR with {1b}, giving {{addend}}.
plugin.gf256.step.gmul.add: Bit {{bit}} of b is 1, so add {{addend}} to the accumulator: {{acc}}.
plugin.gf256.step.gmul.skip: Bit {{bit}} of b is 0, so the accumulator stays {{acc}}.
plugin.gf256.step.gmul.result: All eight bits of b are done: {{a}} • {{b}} = {{result}}.
plugin.gf256.step.ginv.load: We compute the multiplicative inverse of {{a}} as a²⁵⁴ by square-and-multiply, starting from a¹ = {{a}}.
plugin.gf256.step.ginv.loadZero: a = {{a}} is special: zero has no multiplicative inverse (every power of {00} is {00}), so we skip square-and-multiply and apply a convention.
plugin.gf256.step.ginv.multiply: Multiply by a: a^{{previous}} • a = {{left}} • {{a}} = a^{{exponent}} = {{value}}.
plugin.gf256.step.ginv.result: Since a²⁵⁵ = {01}, a²⁵⁴ is the multiplicative inverse: {{a}}⁻¹ = {{result}}.
plugin.gf256.step.ginv.resultZero: {00} has no multiplicative inverse; by convention its inverse is defined as {00}.
plugin.gf256.formula.gmulLoad: a • b = ⊕ a • xⁱ over all set bits i of b
plugin.gf256.formula.add: b bit {{bit}} = 1: acc ← acc ⊕ a • x^{{bit}}
plugin.gf256.error.invalidParams: Give the operation and the bytes a and b as hex text.
plugin.gf256.error.op: Unknown operation “{{op}}”: choose xtime, multiplication or inverse.
plugin.gf256.error.aLength: a has {{length}} bytes; it needs exactly one byte (two hex digits).
plugin.gf256.error.bLength: b has {{length}} bytes; it needs exactly one byte (two hex digits).
